speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It does so by allocating a limited supply of COEs via a bidding system.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Those with the highest bid win the right to own a vehicle in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The COE system currently is based on purely economic considerations, on the belief that economic efficiency is optimised by allocating resources to those most willing and able to pay.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This has meant that car ownership has also become a goal that is only achievable by the wealthy, without regard for who has a greater need for a car.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Progress Singapore Party (PSP) is of the view that public policies should not be based on economic optimisation alone.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Social considerations must also be taken into account for fairer and more holistic policies.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In the case of commercial vehicles, PSP has no objection to the current system of allocating based on those most willing and able to pay.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This also means that PSP will support the creation of a separate COE category for private hire cars (PHCs).

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We look forward to the Transport Minister sharing an update on this during the Budget debate in February.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In 2023, I urged the Government to consider adjusting our COE system to take into consideration needs factors, such as families with persons with disabilities (PwDs) or children.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: However, then-Minister for Transport S Iswaran cited various practical difficulties incorporating needs into the system.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: What are COE credits and how do we get them?

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: For illustration purposes, let me give some examples of how we can distribute the COE credits.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: For example, we can distribute 100 credits to each adult Singapore Citizen and 70 to each adult PR.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Those with children aged 12 or below get an additional 200 credits per child who is a Singaporean Citizen; and 140 per child who is a PR.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Senior citizens above the retirement age gets an additional 100 credits.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Those who have mobility impairment, such as those who qualify for Class 1 or Class 2 car park labels for the disabled, can get an additional 200 credits.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In recognition of the contributions of those who served National Service (NS), we can also distribute additional credits to them.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: These examples given are not exhaustive, but serve to illustrate how we can use this system to take into account needs and social contributions and make it less costly for those with greater need to own a vehicle.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Families can pool their COE credits together to bid for a vehicle.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Larger families will, thus, find it less costly to get a car.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Those who want to own a vehicle can buy the COE credits from those who do not, in order to submit a higher bid.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This sets up a system of transfer from vehicle owners to those using public transport.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Foreigners residing in Singapore who wish to buy a car will also have to buy COE credits from Singaporeans and PRs.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Under this system, unavoidably, those who are financially better off would still be better able to acquire a COE, although it is ameliorated to some extent by distributing COE credits based on needs factors.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It is also accompanied by a redistribution of wealth from vehicle owners to non-car owners and from foreigners to Singaporeans and PRs.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It is thus not only a tool for controlling the number of vehicles, but also a tool for redistribution that is self-adjusting based on different economic conditions.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: For example, when the economic gap between the upper segments and the rest widens, the transfers automatically increase with the additional purchasing power of the top, and vice-versa.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The intention of PSP’s proposed system is to: one, lower the cost for those with greater need compared to those with less; two, lower the cost for those willing to wait and accumulate their COE credits as compared to those who are less patient; and three, reward those who choose not to own a car and help them better cope with the rising cost of public transportation.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In addition to the normal COE credits, we propose the introduction of Gift COE credits, which can only be gifted to others, not sold.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: While we try to formulate public policies to cater to different circumstances as best as we can, it is not practical to expect all scenarios to be covered.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: As individuals, we are better able to see the circumstances of the people around us and make our own judgement on who has a greater need.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We can transfer our Gift COE credits to those with greater needs or simply just to whoever we wish to help.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: For example, in addition to the 100 COE credits for each adult Singaporean, we can give 10 Gift COE credits.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: To prevent abuses, we can put certain safeguards in place.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: For example, Gift COE credits cannot be used by people who live at the same address.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Also, once A has gifted B with credits, B or anyone from B's household cannot give credits to A or anyone from A’s household for the next one year.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This system allows us to plug some of the gaps that is sometimes unavoidable in public policies and fosters a climate of mutual help in the community.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We believe that the bonds in our community will be the stronger for it.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Gifting tends to be a one-way flow from the richer to the poorer.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: With the gift credits, even the poorest among us will have opportunities to give something to their friends.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: PSP is aware that if the Government foregoes all COE revenues, there will be a big hole in public revenue that will have to be filled through other means.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Thus, to reduce the impact of the new COE system on Government revenue, we propose that the Government collect a base fee per COE.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In other words, in order to get a COE, you will need to pay a base fee to the Government, plus COE credits, which can be accumulated for free or bought from others.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We would like to suggest two ways to determine this base fee.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The flat fee can be determined by taking reference from historical COE prices and then indexed to inflation thereafter.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The second option, a percentage of the car’s open market value, which is how the Additional Registration Fee (ARF) is calculated.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This will make it more expensive to own luxury cars, while those who need a car solely for transport will find it easier to own cheaper cars.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This makes for a more equitable car ownership policy.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In fact, for this option, we can do it via raising the ARF to make up for the lost revenue.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Even with the implementation of a base fee, there will still be some loss of revenue for the Government, as these monies are transferred from vehicle owners to public transport users instead of to the Government.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: PSP is thus mindful of the need to ensure prudent Government spending.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It has always been a priority for PSP to ensure that the Government’s policies do not over-burden the public purse.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: For example, we have previously questioned the Government’s grants to Singapore Press Holdings, expenditures by the People’s Association and spending related to the Sports Hub.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It is also our view that the Government needs to re-assess how we are spending or collecting money in some areas of public policy to ensure greater fairness for Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In 2023, I asked the Minister for Transport in this House if the authorities would consider introducing a levy for additional vehicle purchases, similar to the Additional Buyer’s Stamp Duty, or ABSD, used in the housing market.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: At the time, the Minister said that high COE prices were not explained by multiple car-owning households.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: However, PSP believes that there is a need to send a signal against the accumulation of multiple cars by ultra-wealthy households for pleasure when these scarce COEs could be more useful in the hands of another household that does not currently own a car.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Thus, we continue to feel that an additional levy should be imposed on any additional car purchases by a household.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: However, in order to be fairer to multi-generational families residing together or larger families, exceptions can be made where the household size is such that the ratio of household members to each car is five or more before such additional purchase.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: (In Mandarin):   Singapore introduced the Certificate of Entitlement (COE) system in 1990.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Over the years, while the COE system has effectively controlled the number of cars in Singapore, it has also been criticised because under the current system, the highest bidder wins.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This has made car ownership a privilege of the wealthy, without considering the benefits that private cars can bring to families in need, such as those with elderly, children, or disabled members.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: PSP believes that public policy should not only consider economic benefits.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We must consider the needs of the general public to formulate fairer and more comprehensive policies.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In 2023, I called on the Government in Parliament to consider adjusting the COE system based on public needs.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Iswaran rejected this proposal, citing some implementation difficulties.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Therefore, today I want to propose a COE system that can consider needs and is implementable for the government's consideration.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: For commercial vehicles, we believe the current highest-bidder-wins system can be maintained, and a new COE category should be established for private hire cars.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Under this system, the Government would distribute "COE credits” to all adult Singaporean citizens and permanent residents every month.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Additional credits could be given to those with young children, those over retirement age, the disabled, and those serving National Service.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: People can accumulate these credits, buy and sell them, and then use these credits to bid for COEs.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Under our proposed COE system, people with greater need for car ownership have the opportunity to buy cars at a lower cost; those willing to wait and accumulate credits also have the chance to buy cars at a lower cost; those who choose not to buy cars can sell their credits to offset public transport costs.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This will create a wealth transfer from car owners to non-car owners.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We also propose issuing gift credits that can only be given away and not bought or sold, to encourage a spirit of mutual help in society.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: With these gift credits, even struggling families would have more opportunities and ability to give to friends.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We suggest two ways to set this fee.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: First, we can set a fixed fee based on historical COE prices for Categories A, B, and D.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This fee could increase in the future linked to inflation.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Second, the base fee could be linked to the car's Open Market Value (OMV).

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This would make luxury cars more expensive, helping to create a fairer car ownership policy.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: For fairness, some large families or multi-generational households could be exempted.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: PSP believes that as our country has achieved remarkable economic development in its 60 years since independence, we have the ability to create more empathetic policies in various areas such as housing, employment, and social welfare.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Since the last General Election, we have been continuously proposing these alternative policies in Parliament.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: PSP believes that our proposed approach better balances economic and social considerations, and builds a system that provides a fairer and more equitable allocation of COEs for private vehicles and better matches our value system.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We hope the Government will seriously consider this model.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Given Singapore's land and carbon constraints, it is critical to manage our vehicle population and usage.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We do so through the Vehicle Quota System (VQS), which works efficiently to allocate a scarce resource, COEs, through a price mechanism.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: In addition, we manage congestion during peak hours through the Electronic Road Pricing (ERP) system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: First, Ms Poa highlights concerns with the current price mechanism but comes up with a credit framework system, a rather complicated one.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Under the proposal, those who want to own a car can buy COE credits from those who do not.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The net effect is people who can acquire COEs will still be those who are willing and able to pay for it.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Second, our system today is a transparent, single price mechanism for every bidding exercise.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: How will the prices for PSP’s credits be set?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Are we inadvertently creating more friction and complexity in the process for Singaporeans who genuinely want to buy a vehicle?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Their proposal may potentially drive the price of credits underground, where the prices of the credits become opaque and unknowing consumers get fleeced, akin, for instance, to the price gouging of Taylor Swift concert tickets last year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: A COE under such circumstances may well cost even more than today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: And to guard against black markets, we will need to set up a whole new trading and enforcement regime, which will ultimately cost taxpayers even more.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Third, the PSP suggested that those who do not need their credits can sell it and thus set up a “system of transfer” from vehicle owners to those using public transport.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: However, our system today already achieves this at the macro-level.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: COEs that are paid by private owners form part of the Government’s revenue, which is used to fund the Government’s subsidies for public transport and other public goods such as housing, healthcare and education.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Fourth, I find it concerning that the PSP is suggesting the Government dictates who gets more credits.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: It may sound attractive in the first instance, that different people with different needs should get different amount of credits.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: How do we pass such judgement on who needs a car more?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: To use Ms Poa's proposed allocation, is there strong justification why a male who has served NS needs a car more than a female who has not, and thus should be given more credits to own a car?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Or that a child under 12 years of age should be allocated twice the credits of an adult?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: I fully agree that we should recognise our NSmen for their contributions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We have done so in other ways such as NS credits.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Similarly, families with children are given Baby Bonuses and other assistance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: For these groups, we provide additional support upfront in a transparent and direct way, instead of through a convoluted credit system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Ms Poa also said that the PSP supports the creation of a separate COE category for PHCs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: There have been similar suggestions raised by Mr Gan Thiam Poh and Mr Yip Hon Weng in this House.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: As Minister Chee Hong Tat has explained previously, this is not a straightforward exercise and needs careful study.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: It entails creating a separate COE category for PHCs and moving existing quota from Cat A and B into it.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: If we move too much of the existing quota from Cat A and B to this new category for PHCs, it would overly reduce the supply in Cat A and B and could lead to an increase in COE prices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Conversely, if we moved too few quota to the separate category for PHCs, it would lead to insufficient PHC supply, resulting in higher cost and reduced accessibility for point-to-point commuters.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: So, how much of the existing Cat A and B quota should be shifted to the new category for PHCs?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Perhaps, the PSP can share with us the amount of COE quota they propose to take from Cat A and B, to transfer into this new category for PHCs?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Ms Poa has also suggested an additional tax for multiple car owning households, similar to ABSD.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The key intent of ABSD is to curb speculative behaviour in the property market.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Cars are less regarded as speculative assets, in part because the COE system limits the validity of use.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: As we have also shared previously in this House, multiple car-owning households are not the main drivers for COE quota.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Fewer than 5% of all households own more than one car and the percentage has been gradually coming down.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Amongst these, there are inter-generational or larger households.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Should we penalise such households just because they choose to live together rather than in separate properties?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Other Members, such as Mr Melvin Yong, Ms Ng Ling Ling and Mr Liang Eng Hwa, have also raised similar concerns in the House.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We have explained that prices are a function of supply and demand.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The increased supply appears to have dampened COE price increases.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: When we debated the Cost of Living Motion in this House in November 2023, Ms Poa highlighted her concern with high COE prices, as did other Members.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Central to our car-lite vision is mass public transport.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will continue to expand our rail network over the next decade.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: There is also a role for shared transport which includes point-to-point services and car sharing services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: These services allow those who need to use a car every now and then, to access car-like services without having to own a car.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We believe this will also be the most equitable approach in meeting the transport needs of all Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Ms Poa, the time is up, as we have only 30 minutes for the entire Adjournment Motion.
